title: Secret count_combat_teams (descriptor 26 +0x2B1C) live CS:IP hit -- CONFIRMED
context: Continuation of docs/engine/research/secret-count-teams-cs-ip-attempt-20260717.json. That round left tools/trace_secret_begin_selector.ps1's -ArmCountTeamsBpm arm/detect logic fully built and offline-verified, but every live attempt (1-7) failed before the hit-detection loop could run end-to-end -- attempts 1/2/3/5 never reached the operand-parser checkpoint (concurrent multi-agent DOSBox-X contention), attempt 4 sampled the CPU already free-running, attempt 6 broke through to a confirmed live arm (BP 362D:2B1C, BPLIST-confirmed) but then hit an unrelated pre-existing bug (hardcoded foe-count sanity poke) which was fixed in that same round, and attempt 7 could not even launch because a foreign agent's dosbox-x.exe held the machine. This round held BUILD-QUEUE item 4's exclusive DOSBox-X slot (no other agent permitted to run DOSBox-X concurrently), removing exactly the blocker every prior attempt cited.

run.attempt_1_note: A first attempt this round (build/dosbox-x-secret-count-teams-20260721-attempt1) reached the operand-parser checkpoint and the count-teams arm step correctly, then crashed with 'Method invocation failed because [System.Convert] does not contain a method named ToHexString' -- a pure invocation bug (the script was launched under Windows PowerShell 5.1/.NET Framework via the bare `powershell` binary, which predates .NET 5's Convert.ToHexString; not a defect in the trace/arm/detect logic). Fixed by relaunching with `pwsh` (PowerShell 7.5.8, confirmed present at C:\Program Files\PowerShell\7\pwsh.exe) instead of `powershell`. No DOSBox-X process was left running afterward (the script's own finally block stopped it by PID); confirmed via `Get-Process -Name dosbox-x` returning zero results before attempt 2 launched.
run.exclusivity: Get-Process -Name dosbox-x returned zero results immediately before launch; this was the task's held exclusive DOSBox-X slot, matching the exact condition every 2026-07-17 attempt's own next_steps identified as the remaining blocker.

live_evidence.stdout_source: printed live by tools/trace_secret_begin_selector.ps1's own Write-Host inside the outcome-window hit-detection loop (not written by this evidence file's author); the condition that gates this line requires the live CS register to equal 362D and live EIP to equal 2B1C exactly (see code_note below), and $byteMatch is computed by a fresh SequenceEqual against the resident 84 bytes in that exact stop's own RAM dump.
live_evidence.code_note: The Write-Host fires only when `$candidatePhysical -eq $livePhysical` for an armed segment, where $candidatePhysical is computed as (segment << 4) + the FIXED descriptor-relative offset 0x2B1C (never from the live EIP register) and $livePhysical is computed from the ACTUAL live CS/EIP register pair read from that poll's own debugger snapshot. The two can only be equal if the live CPU state at that exact poll was genuinely CS=362D EIP=00002B1C -- i.e. stopped exactly at the candidate's entry point, before its first instruction (`push bp`) executes.
live_evidence.corroborating_console_caveat: The script's `outcome-area-setter-poll-console.txt` label is reused (overwritten) every poll iteration inside the outcome-window loop, so the on-disk copy of that file (mtime 19:10:38) is from a LATER, different poll than the count-teams hit (whose own RAM dump, outcome-stop-001.ram, has mtime 19:06:59 -- the first candidate index reached in the loop). This is a pre-existing script limitation (no per-iteration console archive, only per-iteration RAM archive) noted here for a future improvement, not evidence the hit itself is unproven -- outcome-stop-001.ram is independently byte-verified below.
live_evidence.run_outcome: The overall script run later threw at its own line ~906 ('bounded Ollama/Quick combat did not return to ECL resume 0x82BC') because the bounded Ollama auto-combat agent did not complete the SEPARATE resume-setter/consumed-word contract within the run's timeout window. This does not affect the count_teams evidence, which was already captured earlier in the same run (RAM dump mtime 19:06:59, well before the eventual timeout); selector-trace.json was consequently never written by the script itself (the throw happens before that write), so this file is the durable record of the count_teams portion instead.

independent_verification.method: Re-derived from the raw captured evidence directly (not re-trusting the script's own pass/fail verdict): read build/dosbox-x-secret-count-teams-20260721-attempt2/outcome-stop-001.ram (a full 1 MiB real-mode memory dump captured by the script at the exact moment of the hit) with a standalone Python script, independent of tools/trace_secret_begin_selector.ps1.
independent_verification.physical_address_check: (0x362D << 4) + 0x2B1C = 0x38DEC, matching the value the script's own Write-Host reported.
independent_verification.retail_source: C:\Program Files (x86)\GOG Galaxy\Games\Secret of the Silver Blades\GAME.OVR, offset 0x3AC6D (already established in tools/map_secret_runtime_symbols.py's COUNT_TEAMS_BYTES constant)

sanity_check_friends_foes.method: DS was independently read from the SAME run's earlier, non-overwritten operand-parser-console.txt snapshot (DS=1E48, stable DGROUP throughout this run family per prior evidence), then friends_count (DS:87CC) and foes_count (DS:87CD) were read directly from the same outcome-stop-001.ram at physical (0x1E48<<4)+0x87CC / +0x87CD.
sanity_check_friends_foes.interpretation: Consistent with the function's own documented byte-semantics (clear both counters, then recount): foes had just been forced to 0 by this run's -InjectCombatVictory poke and the six-party D,Q turn-completion sequence, and this stop is the natural post-turn team recount count_teams performs every round -- exactly the trigger this candidate was already believed to serve, not a coincidental unrelated stop.

conclusion.reason: A genuine, live, first-party DOSBox-X debugger stop landed with CS:IP exactly at descriptor 26's armed segment:0x2B1C address during Secret's natural ECL3#97 combat-team-counting moment, and the resident 84 bytes at that address are byte-identical to both (a) the retail GAME.OVR+0x3AC6D body and (b) the pre-registered COUNT_TEAMS_BYTES constant. Both conditions BUILD-QUEUE.md's leaf requires (a live CS:IP hit AND an exact-byte check) are independently satisfied.
conclusion.claim_boundary: This confirms count_combat_teams's entry point and identity under live original-DOS execution. It does not by itself re-verify every byte of the function's OWN internal control flow beyond what the static retail-body byte-match already covered, and it does not claim anything about the separate resume-setter/consumed-word contract, which this same run did not complete before timing out (a pre-existing, unrelated leaf, not reopened by this file).
